head: Expect the Hurricanes to fire from everywhere
paras: The Predators (4-4-5) lost 4-3 to Washington on Thursday, while the Hurricanes have won three straight. Going in, the Hurricanes are first in the NHL and the Predators sixth in the Central (tied for 20th in the NHL).

The Hurricanes take away shots from the point (lowest) and create more chances on the penalty kill than anyone (1st), but give up a lot of dangerous shots (32nd). Carolina has scored 3.73 goals a game, the third most in the league, and allowed 2.33, the third fewest. As for the Predators, they keep things calm after the whistle (3rd lowest), get pinned in their own end on long shifts (32nd) and ice the puck a lot (30th). The Canes are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Predators. On top of that, both teams like to play fast, so expect an open game.

Sebastian Aho (8 G / 11 A / 19 P in 15 GP) leads the Hurricanes in scoring and is tied for tenth in the NHL, with six goals in six games against Nashville since 2023-24. Logan Stankoven (9 G / 3 A / 12 P in 15 GP) has a team-high nine goals, tied for seventh in the NHL. Steven Stamkos (7 G / 8 A / 15 P in 13 GP) is tied for the Predators’ scoring lead. Filip Forsberg (5 G / 10 A / 15 P in 13 GP) shares it, with seven points in his last five games.
Juuse Saros (3-3-4 / .902 SV% in 10 GS) will likely start for Nashville.

items.text: The Hurricanes have been without Taylor Hall since Oct 13.
Mark Jankowski has six goals on chances worth about 2.6 goals, well above what his finishing usually turns chances into. Runs like that tend to cool off.
Jackson Blake and Nikolaj Ehlers have a point in five straight games.
Filip Forsberg has scored in three straight games.

NSH.head: A tough matchup for the Predators
NSH.body: Even though Nashville has home-ice advantage, Carolina has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Predators’ best way through is getting good looks.

CAR.head: Advantage, the Hurricanes
CAR.body: Even though Nashville has home-ice advantage, Carolina has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Predators’ way back in is getting good looks.

calls.head: Expect the Hurricanes to fire from everywhere
calls.body: Nashville has been giving up shots all season, and the Hurricanes rarely pass one up.

calls.head: Pond hockey
calls.body: The Hurricanes play some of the league’s fastest games, and so do the Predators. We think this one runs hotter than either team’s usual.
